title: How a model learns: nudging two dials
objective: Learners see that training means repeatedly measuring the error and nudging each dial a little in the direction that shrinks it (gradient descent), that a well-chosen learning rate settles on the least-squares line once the error stops falling, and that a learning rate that is too big overshoots and makes the error explode.

recommended.why: Watching the line, its red error gaps and the two dials move step by step makes 'nudge the dials to shrink the error' something learners can see happen.

alternative.why: Watching the line move versus reading the loss curve: which explains learning better?

assumptions: Illustrative data: 20 weeks of seeded synthetic numbers, tickets = 60 + 22 × customers (thousands) plus noise, not real support data
The model is a straight line with two dials: slope (extra tickets per 1,000 customers) and intercept (tickets at zero customers)
Full-batch gradient descent on mean squared error; the customer count is standardized (mean 0, spread 1) before training so the learning rates behave the same in any units
Learning rates: Too small 0.001, Just right 0.2, Too big 1.02 (on the standardized scale, anything above 1 diverges)
Starting dials: Flat line = slope 0, intercept 120 tickets; Steep line = slope 48, intercept -80 tickets
Playback gives early steps more time than later ones (time grows with the square root of the step number)
checkDescription: At every recorded step the stored gradient equals the analytic gradient of the mean squared error (central finite differences) and each step moves the dials by exactly minus learning rate times gradient. With Just right the error never rises and the final line is within 5 tickets of the closed-form least-squares line; with Too small the error falls every step but stays well above the minimum; with Too big the error grows every step while the slope jumps to the other side of the best fit (oscillating divergence).
expectAtDefaults: m.outcome === 'converged' && m.history.length === 81 && m.stallStep !== null && Math.abs(m.history[80].slope - m.ls.slope) < 0.01

learnerPrompts.predict: Before you press play: if the model takes bigger nudges, will it find the best line faster, slower, or not at all?
learnerPrompts.explain: Switch the learning rate to Too big. Why does a bigger nudge make the error grow instead of shrink?
